transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood SE), Leo Park (Redwood SA), Priya Nair (CISO, HaloHealth), Carlos Mendes (VP Eng), Alyssa Chen (Legal), Noah Patel (Platform Lead)

Auto-generated Summary (brief):
Redwood presented security posture, SOC 2 / ISO artifacts, encryption and KMS options, RBAC/SSO, audit logging, and data residency controls. HaloHealth focused on PHI handling, prompt retention, and firm confirmation that Redwood does not train models on customer data. Action items and next steps agreed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Jordan from Redwood, Sofia and Leo with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here. Thanks, Jordan. We're good.
[00:10] Carlos Mendes: Carlos here.
[00:12] Alyssa Chen: Alyssa, legal.
[00:14] Noah Patel: Noah, platform.
[00:16] Jordan Kim: Great. We'll run through SOC 2/ISO artifacts, high-level architecture, RBAC/SSO, KMS options for encryption at rest, and then cover data handling — prompt retention, PII/PHI, and our training policy. Sofia, I'll hand it to you for the security overview.
[00:30] Sofia Alvarez: Cool thanks. So Redwood's security posture — we maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, those are up-to-date. We log all control evidence and have live audit logs. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC, role-based access control with granular roles, and we integrate with your IdP for SCIM provisioning.
[00:45] Priya Nair: Quick question — is SCIM auto-provisioning supported for group sync? We've seen issues with partial group mapping in other vendors.
[00:52] Leo Park: Yeah we support SCIM group sync; mapping can be customized per tenancy. There's an admin UI and API to reconcile mismatches. It's been fuzzy in transcription but yes, group mapping is supported.
[01:06] Carlos Mendes: On RBAC, can we restrict model access at team level and have audit trails per API key?
[01:12] Sofia Alvarez: Absolutely. You can create roles scoped to models, routes, or data environments; every request has token-level tracing so you get per-key logs. Audit logs are immutable and retained per customer policy.
[01:25] Noah Patel: What's the retention window by default? We have strict healthcare retention rules.
[01:29] Jordan Kim: Default retention for audit logs is 90 days in hosted, but for Dedicated/Private you control retention and can export to your SIEM or long-term storage. We can configure longer retention to meet compliance.
[01:41] Priya Nair: Good. On encryption: does Redwood use customer-managed keys? We require CMEK for data at rest.
[01:47] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, we support KMS integrations. For Hosted we support BYOK via AWS KMS and partner KMS flows; Dedicated and Private can use your KMS/HSM. We'll share the integration guide.
[01:59] Alyssa Chen: For legal, we need specifics on key rotation policies and proof of separation of duties.
[02:05] Leo Park: We can provide docs — key rotation is customer-controlled when using CMEK; our control plane never has plaintext access to customer keys. Separation of duties is documented in our compliance pack.
[02:16] Priya Nair: Thank you. Now the big one: data handling. What's retained from prompts and model outputs? We can't allow PHI to be stored in ways that are used for model training.
[02:24] Sofia Alvarez: Understood. For Hosted we have configurable prompt retention. By default we retain inputs and outputs for 30 days for debugging and quality, but customers can opt out. Importantly, Redwood's policy is that we do not train models on customer data — we do not feed customer content into any training pipelines. We will provide a signed attestation.
[02:48] Priya Nair: Can you confirm that includes embeddings and intermediate cached KV entries?
[02:54] Jordan Kim: Yes, that's inclusive. Embeddings, KV cache, logs — none are used for model training. For caching to reduce latency we store KV in encrypted caches per-tenant but that storage is not surfaced to any training dataset.
[03:09] Carlos Mendes: Is there an option to disable retention entirely on hosted?
[03:13] Sofia Alvarez: You can disable retention for inputs/outputs; audit logs can be routed out to your SIEM. For strictest compliance, we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control all storage.
[03:24] Noah Patel: About data-in-transit — do you support TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS in dedicated deployments?
[03:29] Leo Park: Yes TLS1.2 or TLS1.3; mutual TLS is available for Private/Dedicated deployments.
[03:35] Priya Nair: Regarding PHI: sometimes our prompts contain PHI for redaction workflows. Does Redwood provide built-in PII/PHI redaction or must we redacted client-side?
[03:44] Sofia Alvarez: We offer optional pre-processing hooks and a redaction library you can run client-side or in a preprocessing endpoint. For customers with strict PHI constraints we recommend client-side redaction prior to sending requests, or using Private deployment.
[03:58] Alyssa Chen: From a contractual standpoint we need a clause that prohibits data use for model improvement and an ability to audit. Is that in your standard BAAs?
[04:06] Jordan Kim: Our BAA and data processing agreement have a clause disallowing use of customer content for model training in both hosted and enterprise contracts. We can provide the exact language — legal ping Alyssa after — and we also allow third-party audits under NDA for enterprise deals.
[04:21] Alyssa Chen: OK please send that language.
[04:23] Jordan Kim: Will do.
[04:25] [04:25] Sofia Alvarez: Quick note on audit logs — they are tamper-evident and include request metadata, model variant used, latency per token, and which internal service handled the request. We can export to AWS S3 or push to Splunk/Datadog.
[04:40] Priya Nair: Does the log include full prompt text by default?
[04:44] Sofia Alvarez: By default yes for hosted (30 days), but you can mask or exclude prompt text and only keep metadata.
[04:51] Carlos Mendes: On regional constraints — we need EU and US residency with no cross-border replication for certain datasets.
[04:58] Leo Park: We have region control in both Hosted (regional clusters) and Dedicated. For strict no-cross-border, Private on-prem is the recommended path. We can map tenancy so that specific datasets and model routes are pinned to a region.
[05:12] Priya Nair: For our legal team, we need an architecture diagram showing separation between control plane and data plane, and confirm the control plane does not see plaintext in a Private deployment.
[05:21] Leo Park: We'll provide the diagram. In Private deployment, control plane interactions can be limited — customer-managed keys ensure control plane never decrypts data.
[05:30] Carlos Mendes: Performance question: if we disable retention and disable caching to avoid sensitive data on disk, what does that do to latency?
[05:37] Sofia Alvarez: There is a tradeoff — without KV caching and with smaller batch sizes your 95th percentile latency will increase. We can run benchmarks; typically you might see a 10-30% increase depending on model and seq length.
[05:50] Priya Nair: We'll need benchmarks. Can we run a POC with a small dataset (synthetic PHI) to validate latency and cost?
[05:57] Jordan Kim: Yes, we do POC scoping — we'll scope a Dedicated or Hosted POC depending on your constraints. We'll include perf tests and security posture checks.
[06:06] Alyssa Chen: Back to training assurance — we want a written attestation that Redwood doesn't use our data for training and a technical explanation of how training pipelines are isolated.
[06:13] Sofia Alvarez: We'll provide a signed attestation. High-level: training pipelines are separate infra projects; data ingestion for training is gated by approvals and pulled from separate labeled sources — there is no automated pathway from production request stores into training datasets.
[06:28] Priya Nair: Is there a bug bounty or incident response plan we can review?
[06:33] Leo Park: Yes, we have an incident response plan and a public security page; will share the latest incident response playbook under NDA. We also have a bug bounty program; details on scope are on the security page.
[06:45] Noah Patel: If we do Dedicated, can we bring our own HSM for key storage?
[06:49] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, integrations with customer HSMs are supported for Dedicated/Private. We'll include configuration steps in the KMS/HSM guide.
[06:57] [06:57] Priya Nair: One more nit — does Redwood perform any downstream caching in third-party CDNs that might hold text?
[07:03] Jordan Kim: No, we do not intentionally cache prompt content in CDNs. Any content stored is within the tenant's configured storage and the caches we disclosed, and those are encrypted.
[07:14] Carlos Mendes: For regulatory evidence, can you provide a log of access to keys, and admin actions — basically an audit trail for key usage?
[07:21] Leo Park: Yes, key access logs can be included; if you're using your KMS you have the KMS logs too. We can consolidate for audits.
[07:30] Alyssa Chen: Legal question — if there is an incident involving PHI, what's the breach notification SLA?
[07:36] Jordan Kim: Our standard is 72 hours for incidents that meet breach criteria; we also have expedited channels for high-severity incidents. We'll include the exact SLA language in the security packet.
[07:47] Priya Nair: Great. That covers most of it. Let's recap next steps.
[07:51] Jordan Kim: Recap: Jordan to send SOC2 and ISO artifacts plus signed attestation about no-training on customer data; Sofia to send KMS/HSM integration guide, SSO/SCIM config examples, and the control plane/data plane diagram; we'll propose dates for a technical deep dive and POC scope; HaloHealth to send PHI use-case list and residency requirements. Any additions?
[08:09] Priya Nair: That matches. Also we want the BAA language and ability to request an audit under NDA.
[08:14] Alyssa Chen: Yes please include the contract language.
[08:16] Jordan Kim: We'll attach those. Thanks all for your time.
[08:20] Carlos Mendes: Thanks.
[08:22] Noah Patel: Appreciate it.
[08:24] [End of meeting]

Notes on transcription quality: speaker labels sometimes overlap, a few words are fuzzy (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K-V cash'). Attestation and legal language to be provided as separate artifacts.
